title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 3rd District
area: South-central Connecticut, including New Haven, Milford, and the lower Naugatuck Valley

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled after only one candidate qualified for each party's ballot line. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+8 based on 2024 presidential results.

summary.text: Rosa DeLauro is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 1990. She serves on the House Appropriations Committee, which she chaired from 2021 to 2022 and on which she has been ranking member.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Marymount College and a graduate degree from Columbia University; also studied at the London School of Economics.
Before Congress, worked as campaign manager for New Haven Mayor Frank Logue and on the staff of U.S. Senator Christopher Dodd, and served as executive director of EMILY's List.
Has represented Connecticut's 3rd District in the U.S. House since 1991, currently serving her 18th term.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies subcommittee, in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Chaired the full House Appropriations Committee in the 2021–2022 Congress and chaired its Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies subcommittee during that period.
Served as ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee in the 2023–2024 Congress.
